Envelope detection keys off the github_core.output emitter call rather than a Success field, because flat producers can carry their own top-level Success key (test_pr_merge_ready.py does).

workLog.activity: Third hardening pass on the coverage guard
workLog.finding: Spec validation found the invocation-coverage guard could still be masked: it compared parsed paths against jq invocation count, and a multi-path program supplies enough paths to cover for a sibling the parser never read. Reproduced at 2 invocations / 2 paths / 1 program, where the old comparison read the line as fully reached. Now compares programs to invocations plus a pathless-program check. Three findings, all verified against the code and all real. (1) The 'two disabled gates' claim was half wrong: the disarm gate tests TIER != T1, so UNKNOWN made it fire always rather than never. That third one is real but out of scope here: get_pr_context.py emits author as a login string with no bot flag, and it is fetched after the TIER call, so closing it means either a producer change or a login heuristic plus a fetch reorder. workLog.activity: Closed a fourth instance of the aggregate-over-the-line bug
workLog.finding: Copilot found that extract_field_reads bound every jq path on a logical line to the first producer on that line, so a line with two producer pipelines checked its second read against the first producer's schema. The invocation-coverage guard permits several jq commands per line, so the hole was reachable. Fixed by pairing each jq program with the window of text that feeds it, breaking ties inside the window toward the nearer of a direct invocation and a captured-variable reference. Two regression cases added; restoring the per-line binding fails both and nothing else. Also hardened the runtime harness after two further Copilot findings: every case now asserts exit 0 and empty stderr rather than one case asserting the status, and the negative control requires exactly one occurrence to mutate instead of replacing all.

workLog.activity: Closed a fail-open the runtime suite had codified as correct
workLog.finding: Copilot found that a tier producer emitting no valid payload still let the loop act. Without pipefail jq masks the failure, and the shapes disagree: empty stdout (crash or unparseable JSON) leaves TIER empty while a JSON error object leaves it UNKNOWN. Both skip the T3/T4 breaker and satisfy TIER != T1, so the loop stripped auto-merge and continued without a tier. Worse, the PRODUCER_FAILURE runtime case asserted exactly that as expected behavior. Statically binds every jq read in the command body to its producer script, derives each producer's real output shape with ast, and fails on any envelope-level or field-name mismatch. Negative controls for both envelope directions, unknown fields on both producer styles, a violation reached through a captured shell variable, and one in the second path of a multi-path program. Coverage guards: every read binds to a producer, the extractor reaches every jq invocation, wrapped payload keys are derivable, the annotated-assignment form resolves, each read binds to the producer feeding its own invocation, and every consumed producer carries an envelope pin. patterns.pattern: Derive a producer's output schema statically and check consumers against it
patterns.context: Shell command bodies read producer JSON through jq. A wrong path yields null, the // default fires, and the gate silently passes with no evidence.
patterns.application: Parse the producer with ast to determine envelope level and top-level keys, then fail the build on any consumer read that disagrees.

patterns.pattern: Marker-delimited shell blocks make a prose command executable under test
patterns.context: A command body is markdown, so its shell is documentation until something runs it. Marker comments carve out a block that a test can extract from every generated copy.
patterns.application: Wrap the block in start/end comments, extract between them, stub the helper functions and producer scripts, run under bash -c, and parameterize over the source and each generated mirror so a stale mirror fails.

avoidances.antipattern: Trusting a PR body's description of completed work without reading the diff
avoidances.consequence: PR #5175's body described a fix, a regenerated mirror, and a new test against a branch whose diff was empty. Reviewing the prose would have approved nothing.
avoidances.correction: Check git diff against the merge base before reading the description.

avoidances.antipattern: Using a Success field to detect the Data envelope
avoidances.consequence: test_pr_merge_ready.py emits a flat object that carries its own top-level Success key, so a Success probe misclassifies it as enveloped and the check inverts.
avoidances.correction: Key envelope detection off the github_core.output emitter call, which is the thing that actually wraps the payload.

avoidances.antipattern: Fixing a silent-fallback bug at the instance instead of the class
avoidances.consequence: The issue #5094 repair moved the read to the right producer but kept the wrong envelope, reproducing the identical silent-UNKNOWN defect one script over.
avoidances.correction: Ship a gate covering every read of the same shape, not only the one that was reported.

avoidances.antipattern: Building a coverage guard on the same regex as the thing it guards
avoidances.consequence: test_extractor_reaches_every_jq_invocation first reused _JQ_PROGRAM. Mutating that pattern to match nothing blinded the extractor and the guard together, so the guard passed vacuously and certified the blindness it exists to catch.
avoidances.correction: Detect with an independent, weaker pattern (_JQ_TOKEN spots the word jq). Prove the decoupling by re-running the mutation and watching the guard fail.

avoidances.antipattern: Choosing a coverage comparison a sibling item can balance out
avoidances.consequence: The invocation guard was wrong three times in the same way: line presence let a second jq command hide behind a parsed first; path count let a multi-path program cover for an unread sibling. Each version looked like it counted the right thing.
avoidances.correction: Compare at the granularity of the thing that must be checked, one row per invocation, not an aggregate over the line. Prove it by restoring the old comparison and watching a named test fail.

avoidances.antipattern: Describing a stuck sentinel as 'the gate turns off' without reading each comparison
avoidances.consequence: TIER=UNKNOWN was written up as disabling both downstream gates. It disabled the one testing equality (TIER = T3/T4) and stuck ON the one testing inequality (TIER != T1), which stripped auto-merge from every armed PR including genuine T1s. The write-up shipped in five artifacts before a reviewer caught it.
avoidances.correction: For a sentinel that reaches more than one branch, tabulate the sentinel against each condition before describing the impact. Equality and inequality tests on the same stuck value fail in opposite directions.

avoidances.antipattern: Declaring a gap unreachable without searching the repository for the technique
avoidances.consequence: A known limit in the QA report and the PR body claimed behavioral verification of the two gates 'needs the live PR loop, not a static gate', and asked reviewers to accept that. tests/test_pr_autofix_late_live_state_gate.py already extracted a marked block from this same command, faked the producer scripts, and ran it under bash -c. The claim was an absence asserted from no search, and it shipped through three review rounds before a bot filed it as a suppressed finding.
avoidances.correction: An absence claim needs a search, the same as a presence claim, and it is the more dangerous of the two because nothing later trips over it. Before writing that something cannot be tested here, grep the test tree for the shape you say is missing.
